newsitem.title: DUBAI: SOCCER-IRAN BEAT THAILAND TO KEEP ASIAN CUP HOPES ALIVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-IRAN BEAT THAILAND TO KEEP ASIAN CUP HOPES ALIVE.

text.p: Triple champions Iran kept their hopes of qualifying for the Asian Cup quarter-finals alive with a 3-1 win over Thailand in a group B match on Sunday.
Thailand's second consecutive defeat means they are all but out of the 12-nation championship.
Both teams had made a losing start to the campaign, Iran going down to Iraq 2-1 and Thailand being hammered 6-0 by Saudi Arabia on Thursday.
Thailand had the early chances, with Worrawi Srimaka, who had caused a few problems to the Iranian defence, hitting the bar with a fierce shot from just outside the area.
Thai goalkeeper Nipon Malanont, diving to his right, was on hand to save from Hamid Rezaestili four minutes later.

Iranian defender Naeim Sadavi broke the deadlock in the 37th minute with a spectacular drive from outside the penalty area. He ran on to a mis-controlled ball by striker Ali Daei and fired a first-time low shot that went in off Malanont's right post.
Daei twice came close to increasing the lead early in the second half before Mehrdad Minavand made it 2-0 in the 54th minute.
Recieving the ball on the right flank, he dummied and cut in across two defenders before firing a shot into the top left corner of Malanont's goal.
Daei continued to give the Thai defence problems with his speed and strength and in the 70th minute his hard work was repaid.
He controlled a pass from substitute Khodad Azizi on the edge of the area and slotted his shot into the left corner of the goal.
Forward Kiatisk Senamuang scored a consolation goal for Thailand with 10 minutes to go.

Iran: 22-Nima Nakisa, 2-Naeim Sadavi (24-Ali Mirazaosiavari 88), 3-Ali Akbar Ostadasadli, 4-Karim Bagheri, 5-Mohammad Peiravang, 7-Ali Reza Mansourian (20-Darrioush Yazdani 68), 8-Mojraba Moharrami, 9-Hamid Rezaestili, 10-Ali Daei, 21-Seyed Ali Mousavi (11-Khodad Azizi 60), 25-Mehrdad Minrdad.

Thailand: 18-Nipon Malanont, 2-Kritsada Piandit, 6-Sanor Longsawang, 7-Natee Tongsukkao, 9-Natipong Sritong-In, 12-Surachai Jaturapattarapong, 13-Kiatisuk Senamuang, 14-Worrawooi Srimaka (20-Phithaya Santawong 86), 17-Dusit Chalermsan, 19-Surachai Jirasirichote, 25-Sujja Sirikeat.
